text: Most Algarve clubs that publish a target expect **18 holes to take between 4 hours 20 minutes and 4 hours 40 minutes**, and 4 hours 30 minutes is the most common figure. Nine holes should take about 2 hours. On a busy day it can take longer: rounds of five hours or more are one of the complaints golfers make most often in reviews of Algarve courses.
This guide shows the official pace-of-play targets course by course, why rounds run slow, and how to plan your day around your tee time. **Last checked: November 2026.**

text: Vilamoura Golf is the only one we found that allows more than 4 hours 30 minutes, with 4 hours 40 minutes for 18 holes. Quinta da Ria and Quinta de Cima are the strictest, with 2 hours 10 minutes for each nine. Monte Rei also spaces its tee times 12 minutes apart, and Ombria and Boavista 10 minutes apart.
What golfers say

We read through a large number of golfers' reviews of Algarve courses. Many of them complain about slow play or rounds of five hours or more, about many different courses. These are golfers' own experiences, not measurements, but three explanations come up again and again:
**No marshal or ranger in sight.** Groups waiting on every tee, with nobody on the course to move slow players on.
**Playing behind a society, a tournament or a corporate day.** Big groups, sometimes of beginners or playing off the back tees, hold up everyone behind them.
**A busy course.** Golfers playing at the busiest times of year mention waiting at every hole. Spring and autumn are the Algarve's high season for golf, when green fees are also at their highest.
The good news is in the reviews too: some golfers note that, after slow first holes, the groups spread out and they got round in just over 4 hours.
Why a round can take longer

**Everyone plays in four-balls.** Algarve tee times are usually for groups of four, and clubs fill them up. Vilamoura Golf always pairs players into four-balls, Vale do Lobo and Benamor make up flights as four-balls, and Pestana's courses switch to four-balls at peak times. A four-ball is slower than a two-ball, so expect a four-ball pace even if you book as a couple.
**Tee times are close together.** With groups starting every 10 to 12 minutes, one slow group affects everyone behind it.
How to get round faster
**Book an early tee time.** The first groups of the day have nobody in front of them, so they set their own pace.
**Avoid the busiest weeks if you can.** Our guide to [the best time to play golf in the Algarve](/guide/algarve-golf-season-best-time-to-play-golf) shows how the seasons work.

**Pick up when the hole is gone.** Pine Cliffs, for example, makes players pick up their ball once they reach double par on a hole. Playing Stableford, where you can pick up once you can't score, does the same job.
**Let faster groups through.** Pestana's, Vilamoura Golf's and Benamor's rules all ask you to let the group behind play through if you're holding them up or there's a free hole ahead.

**Play nine holes.** If you're short of time or energy, a 9-hole round takes about 2 hours. Pine Cliffs, Balaia, Penina Resort and Vale de Milho are 9-hole courses; see [the Algarve's 9-hole courses](/algarve-9-hole-courses).
Planning your day

Add the time before and after the round to the round itself. Quinta do Lago, Quinta da Ria and Quinta do Vale ask you to **check in 30 minutes before** your tee time, and say that if you're late you may lose it without a refund. At Pestana's courses you must report to the starter at least 5 minutes before your tee time, or you lose it.

So for a 4h30 round, allow about **5 hours from check-in to the 18th green**, plus time to warm up, get to the course and have lunch. If you're playing late in the day, check the light: our [twilight golf guide](/guide/twilight-golf-in-the-algarve) shows the latest tee time each month that still lets you finish 18 holes, and our guide to [golf near Faro Airport](/guide/golf-near-faro-airport) works through a round on the day you fly home.
Pace of play in the Algarve: common questions
How long does 18 holes take in the Algarve?
Clubs that publish a target allow between 4 hours 20 minutes and 4 hours 40 minutes, most often 4 hours 30 minutes. On busy days, golfers report rounds of five hours or more.
How long does 9 holes take?
About 2 hours. Pine Cliffs allows 2 hours, Quinta da Ria 2 hours 10 minutes for each nine and Quinta do Vale up to 2 hours 20 minutes.
Is slow play a problem in the Algarve?

It can be on busy days. It's one of the complaints that comes up most often in golfers' reviews, usually blamed on missing marshals, big groups or a packed tee sheet. An early tee time is the simplest way to avoid it.
Will I be paired with other golfers?

Probably, if you book fewer than four. Most clubs fill tee times as four-balls. Vilamoura Golf, for example, always does, and only guarantees a group of its own if you ask in advance and pay for the missing places.
